newsitem.title: USA: Judge seen ruling in Chrysler recall case in March.
newsitem.headline: Judge seen ruling in Chrysler recall case in March.

text.p: A federal judge is expected to decide in the next several weeks whether Chrysler Corp. should be forced to recall 91,000 cars over an alleged seat belt safety defect, officials involved in the case said on Tuesday.

Lawyers for Chrysler and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday made oral arguments before U.S. District Judge Emmett Sullivan in Washington, D.C., over the NHTSA's recall order, which Chrysler is opposing.
The long-running dispute marks the first time an automaker has challenged a recall based on a government crash-test standard.

The NHTSA alleges that Chrysler's 1995-model Chrysler Cirrus and Dodge Stratus cars failed to pass a strength test for the rear seat belt anchorages. In an NHTSA test, the anchor bolts pulled out of the cars' sheet-metal floor pan.
Chrysler alleges the agency's testing method was unfair because it misinterpreted the type of test required by the safety standard. The anchors can pass the test the way Chrysler interprets it.
The automaker, along with General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co, is worried the case could set a precedent that would allow the NHTSA to arbitrarily changing test methods and safety requirements.
NHTSA spokesman Phil Frame said the agency did not change any standards or tests. "We have a well-established test procedure and Chrysler failed it, so we asked them to recall," he said.
"It was a good hearing. The judge was hard on both sides," Frame added.
Vines said Sullivan was not expected to rule before March, due to time requirements for the NHTSA to submit more documents to the court and Chrysler to review them.
If the NHTSA wins the case, Chrysler will be required to recall the cars to install new seat belt anchorages and may face up to $2.4 million in fines.
Vines said the automaker was spending more to fight the case than the cost of the recall.
"This is an argument over testing procedures," he said. "That's why all of the other automakers are behind us on this one."
